what_the_review_made_me_doubt: R2 is the one that should worry a next-round reviewer most, and not for the arithmetic. I applied §b3's own external-document rejection rule to five dev filings and then did not apply it to the held-out filing the A1 ruling rests on. That is selective application of my own stated rule, in the direction that made my headline stronger. The ruling survives because it never rested on the item count — but I did not know that when I wrote the count, I discovered it while repairing.

R3's real lesson is the same one: I asserted what two precedents did without opening them. ADR-020 §h3 names 'reasoning about an executable contract in prose instead of running it' as this milestone's recurring error; this is its documentary twin, and it is now the second instance in this ADR.

R5's interior-span-dominates hit is the only finding that touches evidence rather than presentation. A synthetic fixture reproducing the axp-2008 co-occurrence does not weaken a real-filing prevalence claim, but it does mean the multi-code detector is not as specific as §c1's confident framing implied, and a next-round reviewer is entitled to push on whether 1-in-49 is the right way to state a class size at all.
gate_coverage_observed_working: The ledger-line-refs coverage this PR added was exercised for real, not just claimed: it went RED twice during this repair round, both times because my own later edits to ADR-034 pushed the quoted ruling sentences past the check's +/-2 line window (349/367 -> 438/456 -> 442/460). It failed with the exact message 'does not contain the quoted ...' and only passed once the citations were re-derived. That is the rot the check exists to catch, caught on its author, within one round of shipping it.
